question: A 55-year-old female with a history of poorly controlled hyperlipidemia and obesity presents to her primary care physician for a follow-up visit. She reports that she feels well and has no complaints. She currently takes atorvastatin. Her temperature is 99°F (37.2°C), blood pressure is 135/80 mmHg, pulse is 80/min, and respirations are 16/min. Her BMI is 31 kg/m2. Her total cholesterol is 290 mg/dl, triglycerides are 120 mg/dl, and LDL cholesterol is 215 mg/dl. Her physician considers starting her on a medication that forces the liver to consume cholesterol to make more bile salts. Which of the following adverse effects is this patient at highest risk of developing following initiation of the medication?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Medication that forces the liver to consume cholesterol" -> Increased bile salt production -> Increased risk of gallstones -> 80% CHAIN: "Medication that forces the liver to consume cholesterol" -> Altered fat metabolism -> Increased risk of fat malabsorption -> 70% CHAIN: "Medication that forces the liver to consume cholesterol" -> Potential liver enzyme alterations -> Possible pruritis -> 80%
enhanced_information: Initiating a medication that forces the liver to consume cholesterol can lead to increased bile salt production, which in turn increases the risk of gallstones. This patient is at highest risk of developing gallstones following initiation of the medication.
analysis: Initiating a medication that forces the liver to consume cholesterol can lead to increased bile salt production, which in turn increases the risk of gallstones. This patient is at highest risk of developing gallstones following initiation of the medication.
